Senses.Explanation: 法座 is the teaching seat used for a public address. Records describe the assembly surrounding it, Feiyin Tongrong and Yuanwu Keqin pointing to it before ascending, and the sequence of pointing to the seat, taking it, and ascending it. In those scenes the seat marks the physical and institutional place from which the gathered assembly is addressed. A contents-list witness has no independent lexical force; the defining evidence is the narrated ascent and the masters’ own pointing to the seat.
